title: Another low for Dabo Swinney, Clemson. Tigers manhandled at home by Georgia Tech
content:
From 2015 through 2020, Clemson and Dabo Swinney were the kings of the ACC and a mainstay in the College Football Playoff. The Tigers won two national championships and temporarily supplanted Alabama as the sport’s top program.

Things have declined at Clemson since then, but Saturday’s home loss to Georgia Tech in Swinney’s 250th career game with the Tigers was a rock-bottom-type of moment for a program that continued its stunning fall from the top.

Entering Saturday, Georgia Tech was 2-7, prompting a “damn pissed off” head coach Brent Key to fire four staff members in the middle of the program’s worst season this millennium. And yet, the Yellow Jackets had no problems with Clemson at Death Valley, dispatching the Tigers 20-6, raising more questions about Swinney’s future and where the program is headed under his leadership.

Georgia Tech jumped out to a 7-0 lead with 5:34 to go in the first quarter, which ultimately proved to be enough to win the game. The Tigers, who entered the game with the No. 115-ranked offense, found themselves in further disarray after starting quarterback Tait Reynolds suffered a non-contact injury to what looked like his left knee after sliding on a scramble during the first series.

In came Trent Pearman, a former walk-on, who went just 2 of 6 passing for 6 yards before Swinney and offensive coordinator Chad Morris pulled him for an injured Christopher Vizzina. Vizzina, the former four-star recruit, started the Tigers’ season opener against LSU after winning the job in preseason camp but was subsequently benched for Reynolds around the same time he sustained a minor fracture in his left, non-throwing elbow.

Heading into Saturday, Vizzina was dealing with an ankle injury, and his discomfort was obvious as he began limping shortly after entering the game. But Swinney, who has been under scrutiny for not taking a transfer portal quarterback in the offseason, clearly felt like he had no other choice. Vizzina finished 12 of 27 for 133 yards and one interception, doing his best to grind it out on a bum ankle before he took a hard hit on Clemson’s penultimate offensive play of the game and Pearman relieved him.

With the loss, Clemson is now 2-9 in its last 11 home games against Power 4 opponents and hasn’t scored an offensive touchdown in its last two at home vs. P4 opponents. The 6 points were Clemson’s fewest against an unranked team since a 13-3 loss at Georgia Tech in 2007. And before Saturday, the only other times Swinney lost to a team that finished with a losing record were last season against Syracuse, in 2017 against Syracuse and in 2009 against Maryland.

Clemson’s 7-6 record last season was Swinney’s worst since 2011, and with a 6-4 record in 2026, the Tigers have continued to regress.

The Tigers close out the regular season at Duke on Friday and against South Carolina on Nov. 28.
